## Design

### 2026-10-07 – I started this session by working on the schematic sketch for my Starbie project. My main goal was making sure to create the layout accurately while also learning how to use the program since it was m

**0.9h**

I started this session by working on the schematic sketch for my Starbie project. My main goal was making sure to create the layout accurately while also learning how to use the program since it was my first time working on it. Using the guide for week 1, I worked on the ESP32 connections first, then added the DHT11 sensor, two push buttons, power connections, and ground connections. I also labeled the connections so I could keep track of which GPIO pins were being used.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2H9EsPSzdyosvGq7Zo5uYzmHoG9RB6wx/1739a85182bae4f7bdcc742d154914169e45e29ff3ad7072851761ce3bacc4f9.png)
After going over it a few times, double checking my work and experimenting, I used my additional time to learning how to apply the footprints to the components. It took me a few tries but I was able to figure it out. During this progress I learned that its purpose was because the footprints determine how the physical components will be represented in the PCB.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2H9EsPSzdyosvGq7Zo5uYzmHoG9RB6wx/9457389e543389f948c0d03b1a654e78e1731044a2cbe128cd9b9f1f97190c22.png)

### 2026-10-08 – For this session, my first step was making the shape for the board using a bat reference and adjusting the components so they would fit inside of it.

**2.28h**

For this session, my first step was making the shape for the board using a bat reference and adjusting the components so they would fit inside of it.

Next, I worked on routing the PCB, starting with F.Cu. I learned that traces on the same copper layer cannot overlap each other, but F.Cu and B.Cu can cross because they are on opposite sides of the board. This saved me a lot of time since one challenge I had was connecting the traces without making them intersect with each other.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2H9EsPSzdyosvGq7Zo5uYzmHoG9RB6wx/bde27416bc1465b2328656b6740fa3bfe376366a44f2dc4027b8a3f8e4b30e79.png)

 After this, I worked on the GND pour using the Draw Filled Zones tool. During this process, I was also learning some KiCad shortcuts, such as Ctrl + Shift + Z for using the filled-zone tool.

My final step was running the DRC (Design Rules Checker) to make sure everything was working as intended. There were some errors, so I went back and fixed them. This included rerouting some of the F.Cu and B.Cu traces because they were too close to other parts of the board.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2H9EsPSzdyosvGq7Zo5uYzmHoG9RB6wx/0b4978957d5e5a9ab81cf9a8b43fb0e39efe94a775489a23c3ae0d996dab7775.png)

October 8 — Arduino Setup
Time spent: 34 minutes

Today I started setting up the Arduino software for my project by adding the provided script and learning how the Arduino program works. I selected the XIAO ESP32C3 as the board I would be working with and installed the required ESP32 board packages.

<img width="1122" height="305" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b04496dd-860d-4603-a75e-a9ed42a420c4" />

I also installed the libraries needed for the project: Adafruit GFX Library, Adafruit SSD1306, MPU6050, and DHT Sensor Library. While following the project guide, I learned how to find and install board packages and libraries, as well as how to use the different tools and settings in the Arduino IDE.
<img width="1196" height="650" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1810b07-c980-4ce9-9b6a-563ff70beeee" />


This setup gave me the software and libraries needed to continue working on the project and eventually test the provided code with the hardware.

During this process, one fact I learned was that to actually upload the script, I needed the physical pcb board. I had spent like ten minutes offscreen trying to figure out why it wasn't initially working until I realized which I thought was a little funny.
